entries.title: Revelation of John 11:1
segments:
The sanctuary is measure for preservation; the courts of the temple remain desolate, two witnesses appear who are killed and return to life.
 
 A read like unto a rod./ See

.
 

 
 Measure the temple of God.  This symbolizes, as often, the faithful church, made up of God's chosen ones, preserved in spit of persecution.

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:2
segments: Court which is without. Corresponding to the Court of the Gentiles in the Jewish Temple.  See

.
 

 
 Forty and two months. Three years and a half, 1260 days, have a symbolic meaning, which we cannot now interpret.

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:3
segments:
My two witnesses. We cannot tell whether the words have a personal application; they certainly refer to the message of the church itself, the true witness to Christ.
 

 
 Clothed in sackcloth. Because they were to preach repentance and judgment.

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:4
segments: Two olive trees. Supplying the lamps in the temple.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:6
segments: To shut the heaven. To cause a drought, as did Elijah.  See

.
 

 
 Over the waters, etc.  As did Moses and Aaron.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:7
segments:
Have power. God's word is ever mighty for judgment.
 

 
 The beast. The world-power opposing the church; as prophesied in
.  This passage anticipates what is written in

.
 

 
 Shall make war, etc.  Symbolic of the temporary triumph of the world-power of darkness over the church.  The passage doubtless has a direct reference to the persecutions of Christians by the Roman empire.

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:8
segments:
Lie in the street. This was a very great indignity in the eyes of the Jews.
 

 
 The great city. The last part of the verse shows that this was Jerusalem.
 

 
 Sodom and Egypt. Two names which are typical of great wickedness.  In the Scriptures, Jerusalem is sometimes spoken of as Sodom.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:10
segments: Prophets tormented them. The true prophet always is a torment to those who have guilty consciences; as Elijah was to Ahab (
).  So also Peter, and Stephen.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 11:15
segments:
:18
 
These verses constitute a song of triumph, for God has established his kingdom and has begun to execute his judgments.   Thus we are brought to see what the end shall be.
